name: Arkansas

sales.rateNote: State sales and use tax rate of 6.5% since July 1, 2013. Food and food ingredients carry a 0% state rate since January 1, 2026, but city and county taxes still apply to them.

local.levies: city and county sales and use taxes, collected by DFA and sourced to the point of delivery
local.capNote: Since 2008, local tax on a single transaction is capped (taxed on the first $2,500) only for motor vehicles licensed for highway use, aircraft, watercraft and manufactured housing; businesses can claim rebates of local tax paid on invoices above $2,500.

groceries.note: State Reduced Food Tax rate is 0.000% effective January 1, 2026 (Act 1008 of 2025). Food and food ingredients remain subject to city and county sales taxes.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable except during the August sales tax holiday (items under $100).

otherRates.item: used motor vehicles, trailers and semitrailers ($4,000 to under $10,000)
otherRates.note: Reduced state rate (Ark. Code § 26-52-510); vehicles sold for less than $4,000 are exempt.
State Electricity Manufacturing Tax since January 1, 2015.
Additional state Short Term Rental Vehicle Tax.
Additional state tax listed by DFA (code 80-01) on top of the general rate for the covered activities.

holidays2026.name: Arkansas Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: Clothing and footwear under $100 per item; clothing accessories under $50 per item; school supplies, school art supplies, school instructional materials and electronic devices used for study. Exempt from both state and local sales tax.

useTax.note: State use tax equals the 6.5% sales tax rate, plus the city and/or county tax where items are first delivered; credit is given for sales tax legally paid to another state.

facts.text: Act 1008 of 2025 removed the last state sales tax on groceries: the state food rate is 0% from January 1, 2026, while local taxes continue to apply.
Arkansas's sales tax holiday falls on the first weekend of August (Act 757 of 2011) and also suspends local taxes; retailers must participate.
Used cars priced $4,000 to under $10,000 are taxed at a reduced 3.5% state rate; vehicles under $4,000 are exempt.
Selling your old car within 60 days before or after buying another one reduces the taxable amount, like a trade-in (Act 277 of 2021).
Local sales tax on boats, cars and other capped items applies only to the first $2,500; state tax applies to the full price.
Arkansas is a Streamlined Sales Tax member and sources local tax to the delivery address since January 1, 2008.

property.levied: Local: county quorum courts formally levy millage for counties, cities and school districts; taxes are collected by the county collector the year after assessment. The Assessment Coordination Division (DFA) supervises assessment in all 75 counties.

assessment.text: Assessed value is 20% of market value (Ark. Code § 26-26-303). Counties reappraise on a 3-, 4- or 5-year cycle. Under Amendment 79, the taxable value of a homestead may rise by at most 5% a year and other real property by 10% a year after reappraisal, except for new construction and substantial improvements.
assessment.capText: Assessed value is 20% of market value (Ark. Code § 26-26-303). Counties reappraise on a 3-, 4- or 5-year cycle. Under Amendment 79, the taxable value of a homestead may rise by at most 5% a year and other real property by 10% a year after reappraisal, except for new construction and substantial improvements.

homestead.name: Homestead Property Tax Credit
homestead.text: Credit of up to $600 a year on the property tax of a principal residence for assessment year 2025 (tax bills payable in 2026, Act 330 of 2025), raised to $675 for assessment years from January 1, 2026 (Act 174 of 2026). One credit per owner per year.
homestead.applyBy: Apply with the county assessor; the application deadline is October 15.

otherRelief.name: Age 65 or disabled assessment freeze
otherRelief.text: Homestead owners aged 65+ or disabled can freeze the taxable assessed value at the value on the next assessment date; the freeze does not pass to a buyer, and millage changes still apply.

otherRelief.name: Amendment 79 caps
otherRelief.text: Reappraisal increases are capped at 5% a year for homesteads and 10% a year for other real property until full assessed value is reached.

dueDates.text: Property taxes are payable to the county collector by October 15 each year (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday).

facts.text: The homestead credit was raised from $500 to $600 for assessment year 2025 and to $675 for assessment years starting in 2026.
Property tax runs on a two-year cycle: values and millage are set in the assessment year, and taxes are collected the following year.
Personal property, including vehicles, must be assessed by May 31 each year.
The deadline to appeal to the county Board of Equalization is the third Monday in August.
A 'substantial improvement' that ends the cap or freeze is a renovation adding 25% or more to the property's value.

uncertain: Contradiction: the DFA Property Tax Relief web page still says 'up to $500 ... up to $600 beginning with 2026 tax bills', while the 2026 AACD Annual Report and Act 174 of 2026 set $675 for assessment years beginning January 1, 2026 (bills payable in 2027). amount=600 reflects bills payable in 2026.
Prescription drug exemption read in the DFA biennial tax-exemption report (Ark. Code § 26-52-406), not on a dedicated DFA page; the Arkansas Code itself is not hosted on a .gov site.
Local option to tax groceries: DFA states food remains subject to city and county taxes; per-locality rates not recorded.
